cards.details: Chandragupta Maurya establishes centralized control, inheriting the Nanda revenue system.
State-sponsored infrastructure (Dhamma-mahamatras, roads) facilitates internal trade.

items.title: B.S.V.B
items.decryption: Bhaga (land share), Sita (state farm produce), Vali (extra tax), Bali (religious/voluntary cess).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Mistaking the Mauryan economy for 'State Socialism'—it was a mercantilist, bureaucratic economy, not a socialist one.
Assuming the Mauryans used minted coins only for trade; punch-marked silver coins were primarily for state disbursements and high-value trade.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Control over Magadhan iron mines.
  • Control of trade routes (Uttarapatha).

Officials

  • Samaharta: Revenue Collector.
  • Sannidhata: Treasurer.
  • Adhyakshas: Superintendents of trade/industry.

Economic Structure Mindmap

  • Agrarian Economy
    • Land ownership: State control (Sita).
    • Irrigation: Sudarshana Lake (Pushyagupta).
  • Trade & Commerce
    • Punch-marked coins (Pana).
    • Standardization of weights and measures.
